Every expected result is identified by rule ID, repository-relative path, and line at a pinned commit. The harness downloads each commit to a temporary directory, runs all built-in detectors, compares sets in both directions, reports per-repository timing, and removes the checkout. It exits unsuccessfully for any unexpected or missing finding.

The audit covers both positive and zero-finding repositories across npm/Node.js, Python, and GitHub Actions. Findings were checked against their repository declarations and the authoritative sources bundled with the matching lifecycle rule.
The corpus now has 50 repositories: the 20 from v0.1, the ten GitHub Actions entries above, and twenty more across the shipped detectors.

Sixteen are pinned to the parent of a reviewed migration commit: six clean ones where the migration explains every finding (node-sass removals, Python runtime floors raised to a supported release), and ten where other deprecated declarations were still present. Licensing: only repository metadata, pinned commit IDs, paths, line numbers, and one short quoted line per finding are stored; no repository content is vendored, and each repository is fetched from GitHub at its pinned commit at run time. The main corpus is circular: its expected findings were written by reviewing the same commits Offing is scored on, so 1.0 shows that nothing regressed and not that Offing generalizes (issue #740, decision 0013). The held-out set (
) is separate: it is never used to write or tune a rule, and its ground truth was committed before Offing scanned it.

The two repository searches behind the node and GitHub Actions entries above (JavaScript and TypeScript, 100 to 500 stars, last pushed 2021-01-01 to 2024-12-31, not a fork, not archived, sorted by stars) were walked past the last repository they had already supplied. The first repositories after that point that are not in the corpus, are at most 50,000 KB, and have a workflow file are held out: 15 (five from the JavaScript list at ranks 76 to 97, ten from the TypeScript list at ranks 65 to 81; the lists ended at 100 results).

Every finding that appears or disappears between two consecutive releases must be explained by a rule that was added, removed, or edited between them (an edit means any field a scan reads; sources and provenance do not count), or, for
findings, by a change to the SHA map. The run prints each change with its explanation and exits with status 1 when any change is unexplained.

Growing the corpus to 200 repositories per ecosystem means about 4,600 pins, far beyond hand labeling every finding before the first scan. The candidate finder freezes the pins (
); a second tool scans a local checkout of each eligible pin and records what the current detectors report as
. The different field name is deliberate: no scoring, threshold, or maturity function reads it, so an unreviewed entry cannot be mistaken for ground truth.
The tool reads the frozen candidate report, takes only candidates with an eligible immutable pin, and scans

with the bundled lifecycle data. It never fetches, installs, builds, or runs repository code, and it uses no network. Transitive findings are omitted for the same reason the harness omits them. A missing checkout or scan failure stops the batch rather than writing a partial result.
